Rohan — thanks for the heads up. Reviewed the customer request and the attached order form. Recommendation summary:

- Use a one-page Change Order attached to the existing MSA (preferred) rather than a standalone SOW. Keeps signature path simpler and preserves original MSA terms.
- Pricing: we can accept a blended unit price if Finance signs off. The Change Order should include an explicit formula showing the blended price calculation and the effective date.
- Capacity reallocation: include a short clause: "Customer may reallocate committed capacity between service lines up to the committed amount; such reallocations will be effective upon written notice and shall not extend the initial Term unless otherwise agreed." This avoids re-running the commit term.
- SLA/Exhibit B: add an amendment paragraph that replaces Exhibit B latency table for Production line only; do not change acceptance criteria for Pre-Prod (training) to avoid scope creep.

Redline notes: I created a PDF with inline comments (msa_redline_notes_20270829.pdf). Key legal flags: 1) ensure billing proration language is explicit for intra-term reallocations; 2) confirm KMS/data residency not impacted by reallocation (customer indicated no), 3) include a short "no other changes" clause so we are not implicitly reopening indemnity/warranty terms.

If Finance approves blended rate, I'll produce a blackline change order and a short form amendment. If Finance is not comfortable, we can propose a two-step: temporary trial blended rate for 90 days with usage reporting, followed by full adoption.

I'll attach the draft redline by EOD Friday.
